<reflection>
The fitting results from two experiments show that mechanisms M8, M6, and M7 have the lowest negative log-likelihood (NLL) values, but the differences among them and many other mechanisms (e.g., M12, M13, M2, etc.) are very small (ΔNLL < 0.1). This indicates that the data from moderate and low-catalyst conditions is insufficient to clearly discriminate among the candidate mechanisms. The aim of the second experiment was to probe catalyst concentration dependence, which may have slightly separated some mechanisms, but the core cluster remains plausible. Therefore, further experimentation is needed to reduce uncertainty over the entire set.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To break the degeneracy among the top candidates, I propose an experiment with high substrate concentration (5.0 M) and low catalyst concentration (0.001 M), with no initial product. This condition tests saturation effects, which can differentiate mechanisms involving substrate inhibition (e.g., M7: S+catS<=>catS2), deactivation by substrate (e.g., M11, M16), or multiple substrate binding steps. Mechanisms with catalyst activation (M6, M8) may exhibit different saturation kinetics compared to simple Michaelis-Menten (M1). Dimerization mechanisms (M2, M3, M13, etc.) might show altered behavior if substrate binding affects dimer formation. High substrate also probes the reversibility of the reaction, though with no initial product, the forward direction is emphasized. This design avoids repeating previous conditions and targets a broad range of mechanisms simultaneously, rather than focusing on a single pair.
</hypothesis>
